mappings.note: Asks what science IS (a way of thinking, not a store of facts). That is the nature of scientific knowledge, the goal's own words; no LO under CG-SCI1 fits because both of its competencies are about identifying/classifying real materials, which this question never touches.

Jigsaw-puzzle analogy: each discovery opens new questions. This is the 'developmental' clause of CG-SCI1 verbatim. Not CG-SCI2, which is about the learner's own process skills rather than how the body of knowledge grows.

Defines the scientific method as observe-question-guess-test, which is the goal statement's list of process skills. Not C-SCI2.1-LO-1, which wants an investigation actually conducted; this only names the steps.

Student must choose the next investigative step (pose the question) after an observation about plants in the dark. That is planning an investigation to seek an answer to a query, not merely reciting the method.

The point is that everyday problem-solving IS scientific method in use. Applying scientific learning in day-to-day life, not CG-SCI2, because the question tests transfer to ordinary situations rather than the skill itself.
Science as dynamic inquiry versus passive memorisation is a statement about the nature of scientific knowledge. No LO addresses epistemology.

Identifies 'accepting a guess without testing it' as the non-step, so it tests knowing that a guess must be TESTED by investigation. C-SCI2.1-LO-1 over CG-SCI2 because the discriminator is the testing step specifically.

Replacing the flashlight batteries must be recognised as the hypothesis-testing step (C-SCI2.1-LO-1) and it is a household situation (C-SCI3.2-LO-1). Not C-SCI2.2-LO-1: the question is about the method stage, not about the cause of the fault.
Scientific knowledge can be revised by new evidence -- the 'testable, developmental' clause of the goal. Nothing below goal level speaks to revisability.
Benefit of working with friends -- cooperation, which C-SCI4.2-LO-2 names explicitly. Not C-SCI4.2-LO-1, which is about creativity in designing and planning.
Terminology of the investigative cycle (hypothesis = untested guess). Belongs with conducting investigations rather than CG-SCI2 because it names one specific stage instrument.
'A wise person is a whys person' is about posing questions, which appears in the CG-SCI2 goal text. No LO covers question-posing as a disposition.
Asks which scientific QUESTION follows from a seasonal-bird observation. Question-posing from observation is goal-level; not C-SCI2.2-LO-1, since no cause is asked for, only the question.
Where science is found (ocean depths to outer space) -- the 'unified' clause of CG-SCI1, that one body of knowledge spans all scales.
Moving a puzzle piece = science self-correcting when evidence changes. Nature of scientific knowledge; no LO reaches this.
The aim of asking questions and exploring. Goal-level process disposition, not an LO about a specific investigation.

Bicycle repair air leak illustrates the scientific approach in an everyday trade. Day-to-day application, chosen over C-SCI2.1-LO-1 because the question's point is WHO uses the method, not how it runs.
Recall that Science is the new Middle Stage subject. Purely orientational; cited at goal level because no competency or LO covers course structure.
Curiosity as the quality science needs = scientific temper, the opening clause of CG-SCI1.
Title of the Grade 6 book ('Curiosity'). Book metadata rather than science; cited at goal level for scientific temper because no LO applies at all.
Name a mystery of nature science unravels (why stars shine). A why-question about a phenomenon; CG-SCI2 rather than C-SCI2.2-LO-2 because the student names the question, not the explanation.
Science is everywhere -- the unity of scientific knowledge across domains, goal level.
Whether discoveries change understanding: the developmental nature of scientific knowledge.
Earth as the only planet known to support life -- the 'concern for life' clause of CG-SCI4. Not C-SCI4.1-LO-1, which demands the student actually make protective efforts; this only recalls the fact.
Water as a survival need alongside food. C-SCI3.2-LO-1 covers everyday application including food and drink choices; not CG-SCI4, since nothing about conservation is asked.
Cooling water to ice -- explaining a change-of-state phenomenon. C-SCI2.2-LO-2 (explain processes) rather than -LO-1 (relate to causes), because the answer states what happens, not why.
Heating water to steam, the companion phenomenon to the previous item; same reasoning, explanation of a process rather than its cause.
The pen that stops writing is the book's everyday exemplar for applying the method; day-to-day application rather than the method's internals.
The step after observing is to wonder and pose a question. Question-posing sits in the CG-SCI2 goal text, not in any LO.
Who follows the scientific method -- scientists. Nature-of-science vocabulary, goal level.
Whether an ordinary person applying the method in daily life works like a scientist. Transfer to day-to-day life is exactly C-SCI3.2-LO-1.
Be curious and OBSERVE surroundings keenly. Observing is the first process skill named in CG-SCI2; no LO is about observation as a habit.
Curiosity produces 'how' and 'why' questions -- posing questions, goal level.
Science as a team effort: cooperation, named in C-SCI4.2-LO-2. Not the creativity LO beside it.
The 'whys person' formula again, tested as recall; question-posing at goal level.
Define science. A definition of the discipline is nature-of-science, CG-SCI1.
Why the book is called Curiosity -- scientific temper as the precondition for inquiry.
Two natural phenomena science explains (stars shining, a flower blooming). C-SCI2.2-LO-2 is the explain-phenomena outcome; CG-SCI1 would lose the phenomenon content.
Food and cuisines of India as a subject of everyday science. Day-to-day application; no LO on food composition exists in this frame.
Asks what QUESTIONS about water the chapter invites (why it rains, how water changes form). The deliverable is questions, so CG-SCI2, not the explain-phenomena LO.
Name three materials we use (paper, metal key, plastic ruler, rubber eraser). Identifying materials is C-SCI1.1-LO-1; not C-SCI1.2-LO-2, because nothing is sorted by a property, only named.
Extending inquiry to the Sun, Moon and stars by asking questions about them -- posing questions, goal level.
Outlines guess-test-re-guess for the pen (C-SCI2.1-LO-1) in a household situation (C-SCI3.2-LO-1). Both are earned: the item wants the investigative sequence AND recognises it in daily life.
The three core actions after observing -- hypothesise, test, analyse. Squarely the conduct-an-investigation outcome, more specific than CG-SCI2.
Dal spilling from the cooker as scientific thinking in a daily task. Day-to-day application, the LO's own register.
How learning science improves everyday problem-solving. Application in day-to-day life rather than the method itself.
Advice to ask friends when stuck -- cooperation, explicitly in C-SCI4.2-LO-2.
Science learning as an open-ended multi-year journey -- the developmental nature of the knowledge, goal level.
Science compared to children enjoying the rain: joyful, creative inquiry, which CG-SCI1 names as 'creative'. No LO covers disposition to the subject.
Significance of constantly asking why -- question-posing, CG-SCI2.
Aim of the book is to ignite the spirit of inquiry -- scientific temper, goal level.
Seed to plant, caterpillar to butterfly, as observations that spark curiosity. The item asks for observations that raise questions, so CG-SCI2 rather than the explain-phenomena LO.
Five-mark essay on science as a way of thinking with curiosity as its engine. Nature of science, goal level; no LO is broad enough.
Essay on the jigsaw analogy and how scientific knowledge progresses -- the developmental clause, goal level.
Justify 'science is everywhere' across four scales. The unity of scientific knowledge, CG-SCI1.
Full description of the method through the pen example, including re-testing after a failed hypothesis. The investigation outcome, not CG-SCI2, because the sequence must be executed and justified.
The stated answer turns on collaboration ('ask your friends'). Cooperation is named in C-SCI4.2-LO-2; the question-seeking half is secondary to what is being marked.
Lists the thematic areas the book will cover -- an overview of the unified body of knowledge, goal level. No LO covers syllabus structure.
Two daily-life examples of scientific thinking (cooker, bicycle tyre). Day-to-day application outcome.
Explain the closing 'whys person' message and what it says about the scientific mindset -- question-posing, goal level.
